headline: 15,000+ passengers affected as 103 Dhaka-Saudi flights cancelled
summary: Flight disruptions follow Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, with Biman and US-Bangla suspending services to Riyadh and Dammam.
details: Over 15,000 passengers have been affected by the cancellation or suspension of 103 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia. This follows a series of attacks by Yemen's Houthi group on airports in Riyadh and Dammam.

According to Shahjalal International Airport authorities, 41 direct flights and 59 transit flights were cancelled. Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended flights to Dammam and Riyadh until October 17, while US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled flights to Riyadh until October 21.

Among the direct flights, Biman operated 17, US-Bangla 10, Saudia Airlines 7, and Riyadh Airways 7. Transit disruptions were significant, with IndiGo Airlines seeing 22 cancellations, followed by Emirates, Salam Air, Qatar Airways, and Fly Dubai.

The crisis was triggered by Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which resulted in 13 deaths and 308 injuries. Two Bangladeshis were among the dead and 27 others were injured.
The Houthi group has also targeted the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, causing heavy damage. They claim these attacks are retaliation for Saudi Arabia's involvement in Yemen.
The conflict has sparked fears of an escalating war in the Persian Gulf, which aviation experts warn could lead to widespread disruptions to global air traffic.

headline_marked: Tk 30,000 basic salary demand: [[Garment workers block highway]] in Uttara
headline: Tk 30,000 basic salary demand: Garment workers block highway in Uttara
summary: Protesters blockaded the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for the fourth consecutive day, leading to massive traffic jams and police intervention.
details: Garment workers from several factories in Uttara have blockaded the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for the fourth consecutive day.
The protesters are demanding a minimum basic salary of Tk 30,000 and other benefits to cope with the rising cost of living.
The blockade brought traffic to a complete standstill for nearly two hours, causing significant disruptions for commuters.
Police intervened to disperse the crowd using batons and sound grenades to clear the road.
Similar protests and road blockades have been reported in Gazipur and Sripur, where police also used sound grenades to remove workers.
